sheets.title: Vedic age (1500 – 600 BCE)
sheets.intro: Rig Veda to the Upanishads: texts, rivers, polity, society, gods.

keys.name: Sources outside India

rows.v: Iran – Zoroastrian text in Avestan, close to Vedic language
Turkey (Hittite capital), c. 1400 BCE – Hittite – Mitanni treaty names Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Nasatyas; oldest dated mention of Vedic gods
North Syria kingdom; Vedic god names
Iraq – Indo-Iranian royal and god names

traps: Mitanni kingdom = Syria, but the Boghazkoi tablet was found in Turkey

rows.v: Max Müller (first to call Aryans a race)
Nehring, Gordon Childe
Sir William Jones
B.G. Tilak – "The Arctic Home in the Vedas" (1903)
Swami Dayananda Saraswati – Satyarth Prakash
A.C. Das, Sampurnanand
Laxmidhar Shastri; Brahmarshi Desh – Ganganath Jha
Eduard Meyer
Central Asian steppes (Kazakhstan, S Russia); came c. 1500 BCE via NW passes

keys.name: Rig Veda

rows.v: 10 Mandalas, 1,028 suktas, about 10,600 verses; Vedic Sanskrit; oral before written
Mandalas II – VII ("family books": Gritsamada, Vishvamitra, Vamadeva, Atri, Bharadvaja, Vasishtha); I and X latest
Gayatri mantra (3.62.10) – Vishvamitra, to Savitr (sun)
Farming
Battle of Ten Kings
All Soma hymns
Purusha Sukta (4 varnas), Nadi Sukta (rivers), Nasadiya Sukta (creation)
Hotri (reciter); Upaveda – Ayurveda
"I am a poet, my father a physician, my mother grinds grain"; boat with 100 oars
UNESCO Memory of the World, 2007

traps: Purusha Sukta is in the 10th, a late Mandala

keys.name: Early (Rig) Vedic age

rows.v: Sapta Sindhu – Indus, Sarasvati + Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (Punjab, Haryana)
Pastoral; cattle = wealth; some farming
Tribal – Jana under Rajan; Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha
Nature gods, yajna; no temples, no idols
Painted Grey Ware with late Harappan pottery; 13-room house at Bhagwanpura (Haryana); forts at Ropar, Sarai Hira; horse bones

traps: PGW marks the Later Vedic age; only its earliest layers touch the Rig Vedic age

keys.name: Rig Vedic rivers

rows.v: 42 rivers; Sindhu most named; Ganga once
Sarasvati (RV 2.41.16)
Jhelum
Chenab
Ravi
Beas
Sutlej
Kubha – Kabul; Suvastu – Swat; Krumu – Kurram; Gomati – Gomal
Ghaggar system (Chautang); Sadanira – Gandak; Marudvridha – Chenab tributary (Kashmir)
Himavant; Munjavat peak – Soma
Dhanv

traps: Yavyavati is NOT Beas (it is the Zhob); Vipas is Beas

rows.v: Punjab – Indus and tributaries
Haryana – between Sarasvati and Drishadvati
UP – Ganga and Yamuna
UP, Bihar, MP
Himalaya to Vindhya, east sea to west sea

keys.name: Rig Vedic polity

rows.v: Kula (family – Kulapa) → Grama (village – Gramini) → Vis (clan – Vishpati) → Jana (tribe – Rajan)
Tribal chief, not a territorial king
Purohita (priest, adviser), Senani (army chief), Gramini (village headman, war band)
Bali – voluntary gift, no regular tax
Gavishti ("search for cows"); horse chariots with spoked wheels; coat of mail (varman)

traps: Rajan was a tribal chief; hereditary kingship came in the Later Vedic age

rows.v: Council of elders and nobles; justice and advice; women attended
Broad assembly of the people; chose the Rajan; Rajan headed it
Oldest, most named (122 times); ritual, sharing spoils, war; women attended
Sabha and Samiti – "two daughters of Prajapati" (Atharva Veda)
Parushni (Ravi)
Sudas of the Bharatas (priest Vasishtha) beat 10 tribes backed by Vishvamitra
Rig Veda, Mandala VII
Bharatas rose; later Kuru state
Gotra (lineage); patriarchal
First meant colour; 4 varnas only in Purusha Sukta; not rigid; jobs mixed
Dasas, Dasyus – non-Aryan foes; slavery existed
Veg and non-veg; Soma and sura drinks
Oral

keys.name: Women in the Rig Vedic age

rows.v: Apala, Ghosha, Lopamudra, Vishwavara
Attended Sabha and Vidatha; education; chose husbands
Niyoga and widow remarriage allowed; no child marriage
Siri – women weavers; ornaments Karnashobhana (earring), Kurira (head), Nishka (gold)

keys.name: Rig Vedic economy

rows.v: Cattle rearing; cows prized (gavishti, gesu, gopati)
Barley (yava); Mandala IV; Urvara – fertile field; Langala – plough; Karisha – manure; Khilya – pasture
Wells with ashma-chakra (stone pulley), ahava (pails)
Parashu (axe), datra (sickle)
Ayas (copper, bronze), gold (hiranya), silver; no iron
Barter, no coins; Panis – cattle-hoarding traders, hostile
Five

traps: Rig Vedic people had the horse but no iron; Harappans had neither horse nor iron

rows.v: Thunder, rain, war; about 250 hymns (most); Purandara (fort breaker)
Fire, carries offerings; about 200 hymns (2nd)
Cosmic order (rita), waters; Ritasya Gopa
Plant, drink; all of Mandala IX
Usha (dawn), Aditi, Prithvi, Aranyani
Dyaus, Surya, Varuna, Mitra, Savitr
Indra, Rudra, Vayu, Maruts
Agni, Soma, Prithvi
Rita – cosmic, moral law; Dharma – duty
Chants (samans), mostly from Rig Veda; Udgatri sings; root of Indian music; Upaveda Gandharva
Rituals in prose and verse; Shukla (white, Vajasaneyi) and Krishna (black, Taittiriya); Adhvaryu performs; Upaveda Dhanur (archery)
Spells, charms, cures, daily life; Brahman priest oversees; "kshetra-patni" first here; Upaveda Shilpa

keys.name: Brahmanas and Aranyakas

rows.v: Prose explaining rituals; priests' rise
Aitareya (first mention of the Andhras – outside the Aryan fold, Vishvamitra's sons), Kaushitaki
Shatapatha – largest; Videgha Mathava carries Agni across the Sadanira (Gandak); ploughs with 24 oxen
Panchavimsha (Tandya)
Gopatha
"Forest books" – bridge from ritual to philosophy

traps: Andhras first named in the Aitareya Brahmana

keys.name: Upanishads

rows.v: 108; last part of Vedas – Vedanta
Brahman (world soul), Atman (self), karma, moksha; rebirth first clearly stated
Oldest, largest; Gargi and Maitreyi debate (Yajnavalkya)
Uddalaka teaches Svetaketu "Tat tvam asi"; first 3 ashramas
Nachiketa and Yama
"Satyameva Jayate"
First to name all 4 ashramas
Isha, Kena, Prashna

traps: Upanishads have parables and are older than the Puranas

rows.v: Shiksha (sounds), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (word origin), Chhanda (metre), Jyotisha (astronomy)
End of the period; Shrauta, Grihya, Dharma, Shulba (geometry of altars)
Vedic Sanskrit → classical Sanskrit
East into the Ganga plain; centre Kuru-Panchala (upper doab)
Kuru, Panchala, Kosala, Videha
Krishna Ayas ("black metal") – cleared forests
Painted Grey Ware (PGW); also Black-and-Red Ware
Hastinapur, Atranjikhera (UP), Ahichhatra, Noh
Mahajanapadas, second urbanisation
Hereditary; divine claims; titles Samrat, Ekarat, Chakravartin, Virat, Bhoja
"Rashtra" first used; Janapadas
Purohita, Senani, Gramini, Sangrahitri (treasurer), Bhagadugha (tax collector), Suta (charioteer), Kshattri (chamberlain)
Bali now compulsory, mostly from Vaishyas
Sabha, Samiti weak; Vidatha gone; women out of the Sabha
Consecration – gives the king supreme power
Horse sacrifice – rule over lands the horse roamed
Chariot race – king beats his kin
Brahmins gained power as royal advisers
4 varnas rigid; birth-based; endogamy
Clan from father; no marriage within the gotra
Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, Sannyasa (upper-caste men)
Status falls; child marriage in some groups; Aitareya Brahmana – daughter a source of misery; Gargi, Maitreyi still debated
Grihapati (eldest male)
Gurukula; brahmacharis memorise Vedas
Begins
Main job; wheat, barley, rice (vrihi), pulses; iron ploughs
Still wealth; horses for war
Many – metal, pottery (PGW), weaving
Barter; Nishka (gold), Satamana, Krishnala as value units
Shreshthin (chief merchant); guilds (ganas)

keys.name: Later Vedic religion

rows.v: Prajapati (creator) supreme; Vishnu (protector); Rudra (Shiva)
Indra, Agni lose rank
Cattle god; god of the Shudras
Long, costly yajnas; priests dominant
Upanishads question ritual → Jainism, Buddhism

traps: Bhakti movement is much later (7th – 8th century CE)
